checks.title: Renderer code imports node or electron directly

deny.reason: src/ is the renderer. It has no Node and no Electron access by design (ADR-0004); importing them removes the sandbox that keeps transcript rendering safe.
deny.alternative: Add the capability to electron/main/workspace/, expose it as a typed method on shared/contract.ts, and call it through window.kondo.
deny.override: If this file is genuinely main-process code, move it under electron/. To bypass once, set .jig/off; to retire the guard, run /jig:review.

checks.title: Code that would make an outbound request

deny.reason: kondo is offline by design (SECURITY.md). No telemetry, no update check, no crash reporting — a request here breaks the promise the whole product rests on.
deny.alternative: If the data is already on disk, read it through a workspace adapter. If it genuinely needs the network, that is an ADR and a visible user opt-in, not a line of code.
deny.override: Set .jig/off for one pass, or retire the guard via /jig:review once the ADR exists.

checks.title: A filesystem path crossing the IPC seam

deny.reason: The seam accepts ids, never filesystem paths (ADR-0008). A path parameter here hands the renderer the power to name any file on disk.
deny.alternative: Give the entity a composite id (kind:scope:key), send that, and resolve it in the workspace against the current scan — the pattern every existing channel already follows.
deny.override: Set .jig/off for one pass, or retire the guard via /jig:review if ADR-0008 is superseded.

import fs from 'node:fs'
import { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } from 'electron'

const api = {
  readTranscript: (filePath: string) => ipcRenderer.invoke('kondo:read', filePath),
  listStore: (dirPath: unknown) => ipcRenderer.invoke('kondo:list', dirPath)
}

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('kondo', { ...api, local: fs })

deny.reason: Tests must never resolve a real store (docs/testing.md). Read-only today, destructive the moment v0.2 mutations land.
deny.alternative: Build a fixture world with makeWorld() from test/helpers.ts; it creates a temp home and hands you a locator already pointed at it.
